admin.description: Account allowed to register collections and change settings. Defaults to the sender.

denom.description: The only coin accepted for prices and bids, e.g. "uluna".

fee_bps.description: Marketplace fee in basis points (250 = 2.5%). At most 1000 (10%).

fee_recipient.description: Account that receives the marketplace fee.

oneOf.description: Called by a registered cw721 contract when an NFT is sent here with `send_nft`. The inner `msg` is a [`ReceiveNftMsg`].
Change the price of your listing.
Remove your listing; the NFT is sent back to you.
Buy a listed NFT. Send exactly the listing price in the marketplace denom.
Offer to buy an NFT (listed or not). The attached funds are held by the contract until the bid is accepted or cancelled.
Cancel your bid and get the funds back.
Accept a bid on an NFT you have listed here. (To accept a bid on an NFT that isn't listed, `send_nft` it with `ReceiveNftMsg::AcceptBid`.)
Admin: register or update a collection.

Binary.description:
Binary is a wrapper around Vec<u8> to add base64 de/serialization with serde. It also adds some helper methods to help encode inline.

This is only needed as serde-json-{core,wasm} has a horrible encoding for Vec<u8>. See also <https://github.com/CosmWasm/cosmwasm/blob/main/docs/MESSAGE_TYPES.md>.

CollectionInput.description: Collection details set by the admin. Shown on the collection page.

enabled.description: Disabled collections can't be listed, bought or bid on; existing listings and bids can still be cancelled.

royalty_bps.description: Creator royalty in basis points (450 = 4.5%). At most 1500 (15%).

Cw721ReceiveMsg.description: Cw721ReceiveMsg should be de/serialized under `Receive()` variant in a ExecuteMsg

oneOf.description: Bids on one NFT, highest first.
Bids placed by one account, newest first.
Marketplace history, newest first. Filters can be combined; `token_id` requires `collection`.

ListingCursor.description: Pagination cursor for `Listings`: pass back the last listing you received.

next.description: Pass as `start_before` to get the next page. `None` means there is nothing older.

counterparty.description: For sales: the seller (when the buyer acted) or the buyer (when the seller accepted a bid). Otherwise empty.

Addr.description:
A human readable address.

In Cosmos, this is typically bech32 encoded. But for multi-chain smart contracts no assumptions should be made other than being UTF-8 encoded and of reasonable length.

This type represents a validated address. It can be created in the following ways 1. Use `Addr::unchecked(input)` 2. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_validate(input)?` 3. Use `let checked: Addr = deps.api.addr_humanize(canonical_addr)?` 4. Deserialize from JSON. This must only be done from JSON that was validated before such as a contract's state. `Addr` must not be used in messages sent by the user because this would result in unvalidated instances.

This type is immutable. If you really need to mutate it (Really? Are you sure?), create a mutable copy using `let mut mutable = Addr::to_string()` and operate on that `String` instance.
